# land

Merges head (with its first-parent chain since base) three-way onto target, main by default, and publishes the result as one changeset in one transaction; on E\_CONFLICT, details.report lists each conflict: resolve them with resolutions, against the report's theirs, its full 64-hex id (a path the target changed since comes back in the report's stale). Give idempotency\_key to make a retry safe.

```yaml
title: "land"
description: "Land a change."
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
cli_command: "swarmops land"
envelope_op: "land"
request_type: "LandReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `LandReq`: `swarmops schema LandReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | string or null | no |  | Where the change starts: a first-parent ancestor of `head`, whose own changes are not part of it (anything else is `E_INVALID_ARG`). It need not be on the target. When omitted, the merge base of `head` and the target's head, along first parents. |
| `expect_target` | string or null | no |  | Publish only while the target names this changeset (M5): one attempt, and a target that names another is `E_CAS_MISMATCH`, nothing written; `max_attempts` does not apply. With a `head` rebased onto it, the landed tree is the rebased tree. `swarmops mcp` refuses one that is not a full 64-hex id (`E_INVALID_ARG`). |
| `head` | string | yes |  | The changeset to land: the change's head. A revision as the caller wrote it, for the store to resolve: a ref name (`main`, `release/1.2`), a full 64-hex changeset id or a unique prefix of at least 12 hex digits, optionally followed by `~N` for the N-th first-parent ancestor. |
| `idempotency_key` | string or null | no |  | Makes a retry of this land safe: 1 to 64 letters, digits and `-`, such as a uuid v7. A land with a key first looks down the target's first parents, to `base`, for a changeset that landed with the same key: one squashed from this `head` is the replay, which writes nothing (`status` is `replayed`); one from another head is `E_INVALID_ARG`, a key used for another change. A key not found there is looked for on the other `main`, `release/<name>` and branch refs: one that landed on another target is `E_INVALID_ARG` too, and `details.target` names the ref. |
| `max_attempts` | integer | no | `8` | How many times to try to publish before failing with `E_CAS_RETRY_EXHAUSTED`: 1 to 32. |
| `max_conflict_bytes` | integer | no | `32768` | The most bytes of hunk text an `E_CONFLICT` report carries: from the first hunk whose texts would pass it, no hunk carries its texts (`truncated`), and the hunks' line positions and the blob ids stay. The report's files are bounded apart from it, as `ConflictReport.files` says. |
| `message` | string or null | no |  | The landed changeset's message; `head`'s when omitted. |
| `resolutions` | object or null | no |  | What to make of the paths an `E_CONFLICT` report named, decided without a checkout. Each resolution applies to its path while the target holds there what `against` held, whether the path conflicts or not; a path the target changed since is stale, and the land fails `E_CONFLICT` again, with a fresh report that names it in `stale`. Conflicts left unresolved fail it too. `swarmops mcp` refuses an `against` that is not a full 64-hex id (`E_INVALID_ARG`). |
| `target` | string | no | `"main"` | The ref to land on: `main` or `release/<name>`, which must exist. |

## Annotations

It adds a changeset onto a ref's head and moves the ref to it, keeping all the ref held. Run again with the same arguments, it finds its change on the ref and adds nothing: `replayed` with an `idempotency_key`, `E_NOTHING_TO_LAND` without.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops land`](../commands/land.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Examples

### MCP

```json
{
  "id": 13,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "arguments": {
      "head": "[head]",
      "idempotency_key": "land-7"
    },
    "name": "land"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": 13,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "text": "{\"api\":1,\"meta\":{\"auth\":\"trust\",\"elapsed_ms\":\"[elapsed_ms]\",\"repo\":\"[tmp]/store\",\"resolved\":{\"[head]\":\"[head]\",\"main\":\"[theirs]\"}},\"ok\":true,\"op\":\"land\",\"result\":{\"attempts\":1,\"base\":\"[c1]\",\"files_changed\":1,\"landed\":\"[landed]\",\"rebased_onto\":\"[theirs]\",\"relocated\":false,\"squashed_from\":[\"[head]\"],\"status\":\"landed\",\"target\":\"main\"}}",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false,
    "structuredContent": {
      "api": 1,
      "meta": {
        "auth": "trust",
        "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
        "repo": "[tmp]/store",
        "resolved": {
          "[head]": "[head]",
          "main": "[theirs]"
        }
      },
      "ok": true,
      "op": "land",
      "result": {
        "attempts": 1,
        "base": "[c1]",
        "files_changed": 1,
        "landed": "[landed]",
        "rebased_onto": "[theirs]",
        "relocated": false,
        "squashed_from": [
          "[head]"
        ],
        "status": "landed",
        "target": "main"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Details

It merges `head`, with its first-parent chain since `base`, three-way onto `target` (`main` by
default) and publishes the result as one changeset in one transaction.

On `E_CONFLICT`, `details.report` lists each conflict.
Resolve them in `resolutions`, decided `against` the report's `theirs`, its full 64-hex id: the
server refuses a ref name, a relative revision or a prefix there (`E_INVALID_ARG`).
A path the target changed since comes back in the report's `stale`.
A resolution's `{"file": path}` content follows the rules of [`commit`](../mcp-tools/commit.md).

Give an `idempotency_key` to make a retry safe; run again with the same arguments, a land adds
nothing.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `land`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops land`](../commands/land.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `LandReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required): the server runs with no identity.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops land`](../commands/land.md#errors) lists them.
